what: CBRE is the world's largest commercial property services firm. It manages buildings for owners and occupiers, brokers leases and sales, runs project management and construction services, and invests in property through CBRE Investment Management.
customers: Corporate occupiers managing their offices and facilities, property owners, investors and developers in more than 100 countries.
money: facilities and property management for occupiers and owners
leasing, property sales, valuation and mortgage services
Turner & Townsend and construction project management
moat: Global outsourcing contracts with large corporations that cover thousands of buildings, which are slow to tender and slower to move.
risks: Leasing and sales brokerage fall sharply when interest rates rise and transactions stop
Net margin of about 3% reflects a large pass-through services business
Office property demand remains structurally uncertain
opportunities: Revenue grew about 13% last year and about 10% a year over three years
Analysts see about 30% upside from current levels
Facilities management and project management are contracted and much steadier than brokerage
watch: Leasing revenue growth and the net revenue margin in Advisory.
